identity.title: Expose selected headless verifiers through dotnet test

origin.kind: owner continuation request and current master backlog
origin.summary: The owner authorized the next dependency-ready slice after PL-0038: reduce custom verification discovery cost with a thin conventional test facade.

state.current_summary: PL-0039 passed standard discovery, direct verifier reuse, D-backed output, CI source, Release build, package-health, structure, package-boundary, issue, and diff-hygiene gates.

objective.summary: Provide a minimal conventional dotnet test entry point for selected existing headless verifiers without duplicating their assertions or creating a parallel testing architecture.
constraints: Call the existing public Verify methods directly; do not copy verification logic or migrate the custom verifier catalog.
Use one test project and already-cached conventional test packages; add no helper framework, fixtures, abstraction layer, or production InternalsVisibleTo boundary.
Keep test outputs under Path.GetTempPath so local TEMP/TMP routing places them on D and CI can use its available temporary storage.
Do not launch the WPF EXE, alter product behavior, change the product version, or expand into maximum-input, UI, R0, or release qualification.

criteria.text: One solution-owned standard test project is discovered by dotnet test and exposes separately named tests for the selected existing verifiers.
The facade directly calls C3DHeightProfileVerification.Verify and ToolRecipeSelectionContractVerification.Verify, preserves their reports, and contains no duplicated verification assertions.
Local test outputs are physically D-backed through TEMP/TMP while the same tests retain a documented CI temporary-storage fallback.
The hosted CI workflow has one no-build dotnet test step for the facade and retains existing custom verifier commands unchanged.
Current restore, Release dotnet test, full Release build, structure, package, issue validation, and diff-hygiene gates pass.

context.summary: Public headless verifier with its own report and fixture cleanup.
Public headless verifier with its own report and source-binding fixtures.

evidence.observation: The final Release Microsoft Testing Platform no-build/no-restore run discovered two separately named tests and passed 2/2 with the minimum expected count set to two.

The facade contains only direct calls to C3DHeightProfileVerification.Verify and ToolRecipeSelectionContractVerification.Verify plus temporary report-path plumbing; no verifier assertions were copied.

Both detailed verifier reports were generated under the D-backed process temporary root; SDK and solution artifacts were also D-backed, and the two initial C-drive bin/obj folders were moved into the D-backed evidence root.
CI adds one post-build dotnet test --project step with no-build, no-restore, a minimum of two tests, and TRX reporting; existing custom verifier command lines remain unchanged.

Final gates passed: solution restore; 15-project Release build with zero warnings/errors; NuGet vulnerable 0 and deprecated 0; structure 68/68; Vision SDK package boundary; issue validation; required evidence presence; and git diff --check.

events.summary: PL-0039 completed the minimal .NET 10 MTP/xUnit v3 facade with two existing verifier calls, D-backed evidence, one CI discovery gate, and all acceptance checks passing.
